Package hadur2.core.memory

package hadur2.core.memory
Opponent memory (stage S3): one OpponentProfile per opponent lineage, folded from each round's observations (MEM-2), encoded in a small checksummed binary format (ProfileCodec) and kept in a ProfileStore by the ProfileLibrary (MEM-1, MEM-3 to MEM-5, RES-3).

S3 records and persists; nothing here changes how Hadur fights by itself. S4's hadur2.core.adapt package reads the profile's tiers and seeds to set the opening book, and S5 and S6's hadur2.core.policy package reads its estimates.

Where it sits in a battle

  1. Before the first tick the robot calls ProfileLibrary.prepare(), which reads the battle clock and warms the codec, so the first scan's load is cheap.
  2. At the first scan of a duel, HadurCore turns the radar's name into a key with LineageKey and asks the library to load it before that tick's orders are made (MEM-1). A missing or damaged profile gives a fresh one, never an exception (MEM-4).
  3. During each round the core reports shots, hits, scans and seed samples to a ProfileFolder; at the round's end the folder adds them to the profile in one step (MEM-2).
  4. The adapter saves the profile at the end of each round Hadur survives and at the battle's end (MEM-3), through ProfileLibrary.save(hadur2.core.memory.OpponentProfile), which writes a temporary copy first (RES-3) and drops other profiles' seeds when the store nears its quota (MEM-5).

Estimates read from a profile carry a 95% margin of error (Estimate, DIAL-1), and Tiers names a capability tier only while that margin is narrow enough. Every count is a float that is halved when its group grows past a limit, and every list is capped, so a profile stays bounded however many battles it sees (RES-2).

Opponent memory is for duels only: a battle that starts with two or more opponents neither loads nor saves profiles (the core creates no library for it).

Dependencies

ArchUnit (ArchitectureTest.memoryIsLeaf, tagged MEM-3) keeps this package a leaf: it may depend only on itself, hadur2.core.port and the JDK, and it reaches storage only through the ProfileStore port, so it can be tested with an in-memory store. No gun, movement, KNN, ledger, melee, physics or model code may depend on it; the adapt and policy packages read it on their behalf. Like the rest of the core it does no I/O of its own, uses no clock, randomness, threads or reflection (RES-6) and keeps no mutable static state (CORE-2). The CRC-32 comes from java.util.zip, which is pure computation.

    Estimate
    A rate and its 95% margin of error (DIAL-1): every input the opening book reads carries both, so a policy can tell "their gun hits 15% of the time" from "it hit 1 of 6 shots".
    LineageKey
    Turns the name the radar reports into the key a profile is filed under, so that every version of a robot shares one profile: "abc.Shadow 3.84" and "abc.Shadow 3.83c (2)" are both "abc.Shadow".

    Everything Hadur remembers about one opponent lineage between battles (the artifact's profile schema): who it is, how recent battles went, how its gun does against us, how it moves under our guns, and seed samples for the KNN views (S4).

    One battle's result as Hadur saw it.
    ProfileCodec
    The profile file format: small, hand-written, versioned and checksummed (the artifact's "Format" section).
    ProfileFolder
    Collects one round's observations of the opponent and folds them into its profile when the round ends (MEM-2).
    ProfileFormatException
    Bytes that are not a valid profile: wrong magic or version, truncated, bad checksum or bad values.
    ProfileLibrary
    Loads and saves opponent profiles in a ProfileStore.
    ProfileLibrary.Loaded
    The result of a load.
    ProfileLibrary.Saved
    What a save did: WRITTEN in full; WRITTEN_WITHOUT_SEEDS when only the stats fitted (MEM-5); SKIPPED when even they did not, leaving the old file; FAILED when the store or codec threw.
    Seeds
    How a KNN sample becomes a seed of OpponentProfile.SAMPLE_WIDTH shorts and back (S4).
